patients.summary: Thirty-something marketing coordinator and fitness instructor, five years out from a total thyroidectomy for papillary thyroid cancer on levothyroxine and calcium. Joins the practice in mid-2024 and has two episodes of exogenous thyrotoxicosis managed by her outside endocrinologist, the second traced to online 'metabolism booster' products; both settle once the extra hormone stops.

documents.title: New patient intake
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to join the practice. Looking for a practice where she can reach the doctor directly. Membership info emailed. Signed release for prior primary care records faxed to her old office today. She sees an outside endocrinologist for her thyroid and will keep doing that. New patient visit booked 7/23 at 9:00. Asked her to bring her pill bottles.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 38 pages by fax from patient's previous primary care office, covering 2018 to early 2024. Abstracted for the PCP:

- Papillary thyroid carcinoma found in 2019; total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection that spring at an outside surgical practice, with parathyroid tissue autotransplanted at the same operation. Followed since by outside endocrinology.
- Postsurgical hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, managed by endocrinology.
- Calcium carbonate 600 mg with vitamin D3 400 IU twice daily since surgery.
- Pap 2022: negative for intraepithelial lesion.
- Tdap 2021.
- Allergies: none known.
- Last physical there 03/2023, unremarkable.

Scanned to Media under outside records. Routed to PCP for the 7/23 visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F here to establish. Prior records reviewed (abstract in chart).

S: Feels well. No complaints today. Energy good, sleeping fine, weight steady. Teaches 3-4 fitness classes a week on top of her marketing job.

PMH: papillary thyroid ca 2019, total thyroidectomy + central neck dissection, parathyroid autotransplant at the same surgery. Postsurgical hypothyroidism. Endocrinology (outside) follows her yearly and writes the levothyroxine.
Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg qAM, takes it 30 min before coffee. Calcium carbonate 600 mg / D3 400 IU BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother HTN. Father T2DM. No thyroid disease or endocrine cancers in the family.
SH: never smoker, drinks rarely (a drink or two a month), no drugs. Single, shares an apartment in town with a roommate.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Pleasant, fit-appearing. Neck: well-healed low collar incision, no masses or adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Skin warm, no rash. No tremor. Chvostek negative.

A/P:
1. Hx papillary thyroid ca / postsurgical hypothyroidism: stable on current dose per endo. TSH, free T4 today for a baseline; endo stays primary for dosing. Will share results.
2. On calcium/D since surgery: calcium on CMP.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screen, she agrees. Pap 2022 normal, next due 2025. Tdap 2021. Flu/COVID in the fall. PHQ-2 0.

RTC for physical next spring, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, calcium, cholesterol, and your thyroid levels are all in range on the 112 mcg. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. I'll copy your endocrinologist so they have it. Good to meet you!

documents.title: Heart racing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, for the last month or two my heart has been pounding a lot, even sitting at my desk, and I'm hot all the time when everyone else is fine. I've also dropped weight even though I'm eating more than usual. I don't feel sick exactly, just wired. Should I come in? My endo appointment isn't until November.

documents.title: RE: Heart racing
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Lisa, thanks for letting us know. The doctor would like to see you Monday 9/30 at 1:20. If you get chest pain, fainting, or shortness of breath before then, please call us right away or go to the ER.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: palpitations, feeling hot, wt loss.

HPI: Started maybe early August, hard to pin down. Heart pounding at rest and at night, hot and sweaty when others aren't, appetite up but about 9 lb down since July by her scale (our scale agrees, 74.8 -> 70.6). No CP, no syncope, no SOB beyond what she'd expect teaching class. No change in bowels. Hair the same. Says she takes the levothyroxine 112 every morning, nothing extra that she can think of. No new meds.

Exam: HR 104 regular, BP 132/82. Afebrile. Looks well, a bit restless. Fine tremor of outstretched hands. Neck: scar healed, no mass or nodes. Heart regular, tachycardic, no murmur. Lungs clear. Skin warm and moist.

A/P: Symptoms sound like too much thyroid hormone. TSH and free T4 now. Not changing her dose on my own since endo manages it; will call their office tomorrow with results and try to get her in sooner. Return/ED precautions reviewed.

Addendum 17:45: TSH <0.01, free T4 2.4. Called pt, explained. Will call endo in the AM.

documents.title: Call to endocrinology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with the covering nurse at pt's endocrinology office, faxed yesterday's TSH/free T4 and my note. They moved her up to Wed 10/9 and want her to keep taking 112 mcg as prescribed until they see her. Called Lisa and gave her the new date; she'll take a half day off work. Knows to call if she feels worse.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Thyrotoxicosis, status post total thyroidectomy.
TECHNIQUE: Oral I-123 capsule administered 10/09/2024 at 11:40. Uptake measured over the neck with a thyroid probe at 24 hours, background corrected.
FINDINGS: 24-hour uptake 0.7% (reference 10-30%). No focal uptake in the thyroid bed.

documents.title: Endocrinology Visit Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 10/09/2024

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for calling about Ms. Callahan and for sending her labs. I saw her on 10/09.

She describes about two months of a racing heartbeat, intolerance of heat, and a 10 lb weight loss she was not trying for, while eating more than usual. She has noticed no change in bowel pattern or in the texture of her hair.

Background: total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection for papillary thyroid carcinoma in 2019, parathyroid autotransplantation at the same operation, hypothyroid since. Levothyroxine 112 mcg daily, which works out to about 1.6 mcg/kg, and calcium carbonate 600 mg / vitamin D3 400 IU twice a day. No drug allergies. No thyroid disease or endocrine cancer in the family; her mother has hypertension and her father type 2 diabetes. Never smoker, alcohol a drink or two a month. She works in marketing and teaches fitness classes part time.

Exam: pulse 102, BP 135/85. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. Nothing palpable in the neck, no goiter or nodule; the thyroidectomy scar is well healed and I find nothing to suggest local recurrence.

Results: TSH <0.01, free T4 2.6 ng/dL, free T3 6.1 pg/mL, thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL. 24-hour radioiodine uptake 0.7%.

Impression: Thyrotoxicosis from exogenous thyroid hormone (thyrotoxicosis factitia). With no thyroid tissue, an undetectable thyroglobulin and a negligible uptake, there is no endogenous source; this is hormone coming from outside. Her prescribed dose is appropriate for her weight. She tells me she takes only the prescribed tablet and no supplements.

Plan:
- Continue levothyroxine 112 mcg daily exactly as prescribed, no doubling up after a missed dose.
- No other thyroid, metabolism or weight-loss products of any kind; we went over how often these contain thyroid hormone.
- Repeat TSH and free T4 in about 6 weeks. Order placed; she prefers to have it drawn at your office.
- I will see her for her usual yearly surveillance next fall, sooner if the recheck is off.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for flu and COVID shots. Screening questions answered no. Flu vaccine IM left deltoid, COVID (2024-25 formula) IM right deltoid. Tolerated both. She says the racing heart is better since she saw endo but not gone. Waited 15 min, left without problems.

documents.title: Thyroid recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH and free T4 back in range. MA weighed her at the draw, 73.1 kg, up from 70.3 in October. She tells MA the pounding and sweats are gone. Faxed to endo; their nurse called back that they're happy, no change to 112 mcg, see her next fall. Taking thyrotoxicosis off the active list. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Refill request routed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy faxed a refill request for levothyroxine 112 mcg, 90-day supply. Endocrinology is the prescriber of record. Faxed the request on to their office and left pt a voicemail that it went there. Calcium/D is OTC, nothing needed.

Specimen: liquid-based cervical cytology with high-risk HPV testing.
Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; endocervical/transformation zone component present.
Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 32F.

Interval: Feeling well. No palpitations or heat intolerance since the fall episode cleared. Weight back near her usual. Still teaching classes 3x/week. Endo plans to see her in the fall.

Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily (endo), calcium carbonate 600 mg / D3 400 IU BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, rare alcohol. Same job.
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck: healed incision, no masses, no lymphadenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, axillae negative. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected. Extremities without edema. Skin no rash. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Preventive: Pap with HPV co-test today (last Pap 2022). CBC, CMP. Flu and COVID this fall.
2. Postsurgical hypothyroidism / hx papillary thyroid ca: TSH and free T4 today, copy to endo. Thyrotoxicosis from the fall has not recurred.
3. Calcium supplement: calcium on CMP.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, your blood work from the physical all looks good. Thyroid numbers are in range, calcium is normal, blood counts normal. The Pap and HPV results usually take about a week; I'll send a note when they're in.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap and HPV are both negative. With a normal co-test you won't need another for five years.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 10/07/2025

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Callahan returned for her yearly follow-up of papillary thyroid carcinoma, treated by total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection in 2019, and her postsurgical hypothyroidism.

She feels well. The palpitations, sweating and weight loss of last fall resolved within weeks and have not returned. She takes levothyroxine 112 mcg each morning and her calcium with vitamin D twice daily. No drug allergies.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Comfortable. Thyroid bed and lateral neck without mass or palpable lymph nodes. No tremor.

Labs today: TSH and free T4 within the reference range; thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL, undetectable.

Assessment: no clinical or biochemical evidence of disease. Replacement is adequate.

Plan: levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged. Calcium/vitamin D unchanged. Return in one year with TSH, free T4 and thyroglobulin beforehand.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (2025-26) left deltoid IM, COVID (2025-26 formula) right deltoid IM. No contraindications on screening. Tolerated well, observed 15 min. Last year she had a sore arm for a day, nothing else.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Recurrent thyrotoxicosis, status post total thyroidectomy.
TECHNIQUE: Oral I-123 capsule given 03/30/2026 at 10:30. Neck counts with thyroid probe at 24 hours, background corrected.
FINDINGS: 24-hour uptake 0.5% (reference 10-30%). No focal activity in the thyroid bed.

documents.title: Endocrinology Visit Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, regional endocrine group
Date of visit: 03/30/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Callahan on 03/30. Her roommate came with her and, with her permission, stayed for the visit.

She came in with anxiety, heavy sweating and swings in mood, which she says feel much like October 2024. Her roommate has noticed that she has become very focused on fitness lately and has been on strict diets and hard exercise routines. She has lost 8 lb in two months while her appetite has been good. When I asked about supplements she told me she has been buying 'metabolism boosters' online. She takes no prescription medicine apart from her levothyroxine.

Current medicines: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg / vitamin D3 400 IU twice daily; the online products. No drug allergies. Family history negative for thyroid disease.

Exam: pulse 102, BP 130/80. Alert and cooperative, visibly jittery. The thyroid bed is non-palpable, with no nodularity or tenderness.

We did labs and a radioiodine uptake. TSH <0.01, free T4 2.8 ng/dL, free T3 6.6 pg/mL, thyroglobulin <0.1 ng/mL. 24-hour uptake 0.5%.

Impression: recurrent thyrotoxicosis factitia. Undetectable thyroglobulin and negligible uptake again point to hormone from outside, and the online products are the likely source; products sold this way frequently contain thyroid hormone or thyroid extract.

Plan:
- Stop all of the online products now. She agreed.
- Levothyroxine 112 mcg unchanged.
- TSH and free T4 in 6 weeks, at your office as before.
- Her roommate's concern about her eating and exercise seemed worth passing on. I would be grateful if you could see her soon and follow up on it.
- Yearly surveillance visit in the fall as planned.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Saw endo Monday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I saw my endocrinologist Monday and my thyroid was too high again. She thinks it was the supplements I was taking, so I threw them out. She said I should check in with you too. Can I get an appointment in the next couple weeks? Mornings are best.

documents.title: RE: Saw endo Monday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Lisa, you're booked Tuesday 4/14 at 8:40 with the doctor. We got the letter from endocrinology yesterday. See you then.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after endo 3/30. Letter reviewed: recurrent exogenous thyrotoxicosis (TSH <0.01, FT4 2.8, Tg undetectable, low uptake), felt due to online 'metabolism booster' products. Endo asked us to follow up on the eating/exercise concern her roommate raised.

S: Stopped the products 3/31 and threw them out. Sweats and jitteriness easing, sleeping better. Over the winter she cut back a lot on what she was eating and added extra workouts on top of her classes. Agrees that was too much. No CP, no syncope.

O: Vitals per flowsheet, HR and BP normal today. Wt 70.4 kg. Calm, engaged. No tremor. Neck no mass. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Thyrotoxicosis factitia, recurrent: off the products. Recheck TSH/FT4 around 5/11 per endo. Levothyroxine 112 unchanged.
2. Eating and exercise: talked through regular meals around her teaching schedule and keeping to her usual class load for now. She was open to it. Asked her to bring any supplement to us or endo before taking it. Will check in at labs and at her physical in June.

~30 min, majority counseling.

documents.title: Thyroid recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH and free T4 normal again, six weeks off the supplements. Sent to endo. Messaged Lisa: good news, stay on the 112 mcg, nothing else. Resolving thyrotoxicosis on the problem list.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 34F.

Interval: Recurrent exogenous thyrotoxicosis this spring from online supplements; off them since 3/31 and TSH/FT4 normal 5/11. Says she feels back to herself. Eating regular meals, teaching her usual three classes, dropped the extra sessions. No supplements. Weight 72.6, up from 70.4 in April.

Meds: levothyroxine 112 mcg daily (endo), calcium carbonate 600 mg / D3 400 IU BID.
Allergies: NKDA.
PHQ-9: 2.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. Well. HEENT normal. Neck: healed scar, no mass, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Ext no edema. Skin normal. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Preventive: Pap/HPV 2025 negative, next 2030. Lipids 2024 fine. CBC, CMP today. Flu/COVID in the fall.
2. Hypothyroidism / hx papillary thyroid ca: TSH/FT4 today, endo visit in the fall.
3. Eating/exercise: doing well by her account and by weight. Keep checking in.

RTC October for flu shot and a quick check.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, labs from Wednesday are all normal, including the thyroid tests. Nice work this spring. See you in October.

documents.title: October appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, can I book the October visit now? Early morning works best since I teach a class at noon on Wednesdays.

documents.title: RE: October appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're set for Wednesday 10/7 at 8:00. We'll have the flu vaccine ready for you then.
